content:
here are at least 4 ways you can quotient a ring in mathlib:

  • RingQuot r (by an arbitrary relation r : R → R → Prop)
  • c.Quotient (by a c : RingCon R congruence)
  • A ⧸ I (by an I : Ideal A)
  • A ⧸ I (by a I : TwoSidedIdeal A, which is itself a wrapper around RingCon A)

this comes up in #39790 where these all give different instances:

  • Bialgebra R (RingQuot r)
  • Bialgebra R c.Quotient
  • Bialgebra R (A ⧸ I)

I am not sure which to use. is there appetite to consolidate toward a single ring-quotient type (up to syntactic equality)? I'm happy to help out with the legwork if there's consensus.

Concerning A / I, it is only well-defined for either commutative A or for two-sided I: so they're honestly a bit different, and it would not make sense to completely unify them (although there is docs#Ideal.instIsTwoSided showing that every ideal in a commring is automatically seen as two-sided). The c.Quotient is needed to define A / I, and RingQuot ris intrinsically "commutative" or "two-sided" since it forces both mul_left and mul_right. For your cases, always use A / I, either by a two-sided ideal or not according to the assumptions you've got on your ring.
cc @Yaël Dillies.
In the past I made an effort to try and eliminate RingQuot in favor of(RingConGen r).Quotient, since we don't have any analogues of RingQuot in other categories (edit: #40423)
Maybe after that we make HasQuotient.Quotient reducible such that Bialgebra R (A ⧸ I) is reducibly defeq to Bialgebra R (I.toRingCon.Quotient)

Filippo A. E. Nuccio said:

Concerning A / I, it is only well-defined for either commutative A or for two-sided I: so they're honestly a bit different, and it would not make sense to completely unify them (although there is docs#Ideal.instIsTwoSided showing that every ideal in a commring is automatically seen as two-sided).

So the correct definition is the one for two-sided ideals, no?
In principle yes; I'm just a bit worried of potential slowdowns. So we need to make sure that there are really few paths leading to IsTwoSided.

Eric Wieser said:

In the past I made an effort to try and eliminate RingQuot

#40451 is an alternate approach that doesn't try to change RingQuot in place
Since this was linked elsewhere, #40697 is the next piece of trying to bring up the necessary API to use RingCon instead of RingQuot
What would happen if A / I were just an abbreviation to I.toRingCon.Quotient?
Do you mean also in the commutative case? This is probably a huge refactor.

Antoine Chambert-Loir said:

What would happen if A / I were just an abbreviation to I.toRingCon.Quotient?

As opposed to being semireducible, you mean?
I'm not able to appreciate the difference in performance between semireducible and abbrev, so please interpret my question in the less stupid way.
I think perhaps I'm imagining that we already have this (edit: yes, I am)

Certainly we could write:

import Mathlib

instance [NonUnitalNonAssocRing R] : HasQuotient R (TwoSidedIdeal R) where
  Quotient I := I.ringCon.Quotient

variable (I : TwoSidedIdeal ℤ)
#check ℤ ⧸ I

And this succeeds!

example : (ℤ ⧸ I) = I.ringCon.Quotient := by with_reducible_and_instances rfl
Another thing we could consider is deprecating RingCon.Quotient c, Con.Quotient c, etc, and having the preferred spelling be _⧸ c (that is, replace def Quotient with instance : HasQuotient)
I agree this is the obvious way to reduce the number spellings of the quotient

Another refactor would be to have

class SetoidLike (X a)  where toSetoid : X -> Setoid a

and refine a⧸ X as notation for Quotient (toSetoid X)
(recall that we do not want to use the toSetoid projection of RingCon, because there is confusion between r.toCon.toSetoid and r.toAddCon.toSetoid)
Why is there a confusion?

(I'm trying something for module congruences, and I get Lean — and then myself — confused because there is no ModuleCon.mk'-analogue to docs#AddCon.mk', and defining it shows a very bizarre behaviour.

import Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Congruence.Defs

variable {R M : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
    (r : ModuleCon R M)

-- fails to synthesize instance of type class `HSMul R r.Quotient ?m.15`
example (a : R) (m : M) : r.toQuotient (a • m) = a • (r.toQuotient m) :=
  rfl

-- fails to synthesize instance of type class `HSMul R r.Quotient ?m.15`
example (a : R) (m : M) : r.toAddCon.mk' (a • m) = a • (r.toAddCon.mk' m) :=
  rfl

-- It seems that Lean doesn't recognize that `r.toAddCon.Quotient M` has a module structure

/-- The natural linear map from a module to its quotient by a `ModuleCon` relation. -/
def ModuleCon.mk' : M →ₗ[R] r.Quotient where
  __ := AddCon.mk' r.toAddCon
  map_smul' a m := by
    simp only [ZeroHom.toFun_eq_coe, AddMonoidHom.toZeroHom_coe, RingHom.id_apply]
    rfl -- what should that be?

-- works fine
theorem ModuleCon.mk'_smul (a : R) (m : M) :
    r.mk' (a • m) = a • (r.mk' m) :=
  rfl
that's because one of the r.Quotient is actually AddCon.Quotient r.toAddCon and the other r.Quotient is ModuleCon.Quotient r
unfortunately they both print the same, see lean4#12967
They're mathematically the same, and so the problem might be that ModuleCon.toSetoid r is not obviously equal to ModuleCon.toAddCon.toSetoid r? (Butrfl shows that they are equal.)
What do you mean ModuleCon.toSetoid? I don't see any ModuleCon.toSetoid.

You're right, I stupidly entered, for r: ModuleCon R M,
example : r.toAddCon.toSetoid = r.toSetoid := rfl
But example : r.toAddCon.Quotient = r.Quotient := rfl works too.

Also, I was fooled by the printed definition of docs#ModuleCon.Quotient,
ModuleCon.Quotient M c := Quotient c.toSetoid.

Antoine Chambert-Loir said:

But example : r.toAddCon.Quotient = r.Quotient := rfl works too.

but example : r.toAddCon.Quotient = r.Quotient := by with_reducible_and_instances rfl fails

I made one unsuccessful experiment, having docs#SMulCon (and their relatives) explicitly extend Setoid, and make the definitions of the quotients reducible, as c -> Quotient c.toSetoid in the hope that it would simplify things.

I wonder whether playing the different game of having only quotients of setoids, and passing the additional information as typeclasses of the form Setoid.isSMulCompatible, Setoid.isAddCompatible, etc. would be workable.
On the other hand, Anatole reminds me that we wish to have the lattice structure on the module congruences, etc.

The point is that for mathlib, algebraic structures are additional notions on a given type, while there is at the moment a variety of congruences on a given type, and Lean doesn't seem to be willing to understand that all of these quotients are the same.

One way we've tried to work around such problems in the past, is by proving results about surjective maps whose codomain is a free variable, instead of concrete quotient constructions.
Would that address the problems you are concerned about, Antoine Chambert-Loir?

I'm working on constructing the graduation of a quotient of a graded structure (AddCommMonoid, Module, Semiring, Algebra) by the appropriate equivalence relation. My pain is that what is done for Submodule cannot be reused for Semirings (while, mathematically, it can).
Though that works with a moderate amount of code duplication.

For restricted products Anatole found an elegant solution (making eg restricted products of rings wrt subrings into rings using the fact that restricted products of monoids wrt submonoids are monoids) using submonoidclass etc
We spoke about this together this afternoon, but he did not mention it. @Anatole Dedecker ?
Ah, Kevin is making a very very good point. Instead of introducing "this relation is compatible with X", we can say "this type of relations are compatible with X"
So we would have a RelLike/SetoidLike hierarchy with classes for compatibility
That said I’m still not sure it would solve all the issues here (the heat is not helping me think)
The question for me is whether we want to pick the canonical form as Quot (RelLike.toRel c) or Quotient (RelLike.toSetoid c)
Or phrased another way; we might want to consider extending the redesign to include merging Quot and Quotient
Can we start by erasing RingQuot? This seems uncontroversial, or am I missing something?
Yes, see #40451

Johan Commelin said:

One way we've tried to work around such problems in the past, is by proving results about surjective maps whose codomain is a free variable, instead of concrete quotient constructions.
Would that address the problems you are concerned about, Antoine Chambert-Loir?

Note that

  1. Many many many of these results are missing: we have (AFAIR) no way to lift a linear map through a surjective linear map.
  2. These can never truly replace good quotient API because we would lose the associated defeqs.

Eric Wieser said:

Yes, see #40451

This (+186 -151) is now ready for review; in particular, it would be helpful to understand if there are easy ways to improve performance (without going all the way to converting TensorAlgebra, CliffordAlgebra, etc to one-field structures)

About Quot/Quotient: while it seems useful to be able to mod out by any relation, that only makes sense when you know beforehand the algebraic nature of the quotient that you wish to get, so that for the mathematical library, Quot might not be as relevant as one would think, and Quotientby a given equivalence relation (so that we know the elements of the quotient and can guess what structures are inherited by it) is probably more sound.

About what Anatole said: I have tried to redesign the hierarchy of congruences from scratch, defining type classes of the form Setoid.isAddCon, etc. but it is not clear to me how far one wishes to keep docs#AddCon in the same form, or whether they should become subtypes of docs#Setoid.

My claim is not that Quotient is not so useful, but rather that the useful parts of it could instead be provided as API for Quot r in the presence of IsEquiv _ r. In particular, this would avoid confusion over which of docs#Quot.mk and docs#Quotient.mk and docs#Quotient.mk' and docs#Quotient.mk'' and docs#Con.toQuotient and docs#RingCon.toQuotient and docs#Submodule.Quotient.mk and docs#Submodule.mkQ and ... is the normal form for the surjection into the quotient.
(the answer would be Quot.mk)
(My claim was that Quotient is useful.)
#40451 is merged, so docs#RingQuot is practically purged from mathlib
(what remains is some unused Star material that I can adapt to RingCon in #40919, and then deprecating everything that is about RingQuot)
